application.name: Campfire
application.summary: Host a group chat from your phone. Others join from any browser. No internet
application.desc:
One phone hosts. Everyone else opens a link. No accounts, no internet, nothing left behind.

Start a Campfire on your phone and it shows a link and a QR code. Anyone on the same Wi-Fi, or connected to your hotspot, opens it in any browser, picks a name and is chatting. When you end it, every message, room and file is gone.

  • Public room that everyone lands in, plus rooms anyone can start, optionally with a password.
  • Direct messages with anyone there.
  • Replies and reactions; edit or delete your own messages.
  • Polls, pins and muting.
  • Voice notes from the app or the browser.
  • Read receipts, typing and presence.
  • Files of any kind and size; photos and videos play inline.
  • Link previews fetched by the host phone, so everyone sees them.
  • Moderation: room creators remove people from their rooms; the host can remove anyone.
  • Save the chat before the fire goes out.
application.author: Prem Poddar

application.name: Duet
application.summary: Listen to music together, in sync, on the same couch or in different cities
application.desc:
Listen to music together with up to seven other people, on the same couch or in different cities.

Start a session and Duet gives you six words. Read them out on a call, let someone scan the code, or send the link. Pick a song from your phone, a YouTube video or a whole playlist, and it plays on everyone's phone at the same moment. Anyone can pause, skip, seek, vote or add their own songs.

  • In sync to within a few milliseconds, and kept there: each phone eases its own speed instead of jumping.
  • Anywhere: phones connect directly to each other. No account.
  • Same room: on the same Wi-Fi, sessions show up by themselves and work with no internet at all.
  • YouTube: play a video or a whole playlist together.
  • Play along with a song playing in another music app on each phone.
  • Shared queue: everyone adds songs from their own phone and votes the next one up.
  • Synced lyrics from the songs' own files.
  • Hand over the session to someone else when you leave, and the music carries on.
  • Chat and reactions, and lock screen controls.
  • Appearance: light, dark, dusk or OLED black, Material You, fonts, shapes and haptics.

Over the internet, phones find each other through a public MQTT relay (HiveMQ) with messages sealed by a key from the six words, and use Google's STUN servers to connect directly. YouTube videos play through YouTube's player.
application.author: Prem Poddar

application.name: LibreChat
application.summary: Off-grid encrypted messenger over a Bluetooth and Wi-Fi mesh. No internet needed
application.desc:
An off-grid messenger. No internet, no servers, no accounts.

At a festival, on a hike, in a building with no signal or during an outage: open LibreChat and everyone nearby running it forms a mesh. A message to someone out of range is carried by the phones in between, and if there's no path right now, they hold it for up to a day and pass it on when one appears. Everything private is end to end encrypted.

  • Public chat with everyone in range, signed so nobody can post as you.
  • Direct messages encrypted end to end with forward secrecy (X3DH and Double Ratchet).
  • Groups encrypted with Sender Keys; keys rotate when someone leaves.
  • Photos and voice notes, compressed for the mesh and sped up over Wi-Fi Aware when phones are side by side.
  • Receipts: sent, delivered across the mesh, and read.
  • Replies, reactions and delete for everyone.
  • Disappearing messages: 1 hour, 1 day or 1 week.
  • Verification by QR code or a 60-digit safety number.
  • Requests and blocking for strangers.
  • Nearby radar: who's in range and who's reachable through the mesh.
  • On the phone: encrypted database and media, keys in Android Keystore, app lock, a Calculator disguise for the home screen, and encrypted backups.

application.name: Loadstone
application.summary: Drop a pin, walk back to the exact spot. No map or signal needed
application.desc:
Drop a pin, walk back to the exact spot. Mark where you left the car on level 3, where the trailhead was, where the tent is. Hours or weeks later, open the pin and walk: one arrow, one distance, no map tiles, no signal needed.

  • Follow-back arrow to true north, corrected for magnetic declination.
  • Honest accuracy: every pin carries the radius you may have to search.
  • Sharpen a pin by standing on the spot again.
  • Photos and voice notes on pins, folders, and a home-screen widget.
  • Retrace your exact path, and get guided with the screen off.
  • Radar of the pins around you, live elevation and sunset warnings.
  • Share as seven words or a QR code; back up, restore and move pins to other map apps.
  • App lock and home-screen shortcuts.
application.author: Prem Poddar

application.name: OAF
application.summary: Open Any File: PDFs, Office, books, archives and media, and edit most of them
application.desc:
OAF stands for Open Any File: it opens any file on your phone, and edits most of them. PDFs, Word and Excel, slides, books, archives, pictures, music and video, in one quiet, fast app. Nothing is uploaded; it all happens on your phone.

  • Documents: read, annotate, fill and sign PDFs; edit Word and Excel; view slides.
  • Books and text: EPUB, Markdown and code with highlighting.
  • Pictures: crop, filters, drawing and text, blur faces, remove the background, copy text out of a photo; swipe between photos.
  • Music and video with a proper player, picture-in-picture and swipe between videos.
  • Archives: open and make zip, 7z and tar; open rar.
  • A real file manager: search inside documents, a 30-day bin, storage clean-up, previews, and network drives (SMB, SFTP, FTP, WebDAV).
  • Apps: share installed apps, even split ones, as one installable APK.
  • Share over Wi-Fi with a built-in FTP server.
application.author: Prem Poddar

application.name: Tune
application.summary: Per-app volume mixer: each app plays at its own level. No root
application.desc:
A per-app volume mixer for Android. No root.

Turn YouTube up and Spotify down, and Tune remembers. Switch apps and each one comes back at its own level. Put a podcast on over quiet background music and both play at once, each at the volume you gave it, separately for the speaker, your headphones and every Bluetooth device.

  • Per-app levels for media, ring, notification and alarm volume.
  • Real mixing: music players that share their audio play side by side at different levels.
  • Learns as you go: whatever volume you leave an app at becomes its level.
  • Per output: separate levels for the speaker, wired headphones and each Bluetooth device.
  • Pin an app at fixed levels.
  • Volume panel that moves the app you're using.
  • Quick Settings tile and widget.
  • Appearance: light, dark, dusk or OLED black, Material You, fonts, shapes and haptics.

Tune uses an accessibility service to see which app is in front. With Shizuku running, it can set every app's level exactly; without it, it mixes where apps allow and switches the media volume otherwise.
